adversarial_refutations.argument:
After expanding the Lean statement to primitives, I could not find any place where `SM.root_independence` is weaker than, adds a hypothesis to, quantifies differently from, or misdenotes the printed "For every generic polygon P and any two of its edges g,h, A_g(P)=A_h(P)". Clause by clause:

(a) "generic polygon P". Lean: `(n : ℕ) [NeZero n] (hn : 3 ≤ n) (P : LabelledTuple n) (hP : Generic P)`. `LabelledTuple n := ZMod n → ℝ×ℝ` is exactly the printed labelled tuple (ℝ²)^n with indices in ℤ/n; `3 ≤ n` is the printed "Let n ≥ 3" of def:polygon. `[NeZero n]` is a Prop-class instance implied by `hn` (proof-irrelevant, always constructible for n ≥ 3), so it is not a real extra hypothesis. Stating the theorem on labelled representatives is expressly licensed by the printed remark [formalization] ("A formalization may work with labelled tuples throughout ... the statements below are written so that both readings agree"), and the printed A_g(P) is itself defined on a representative with root index g (def:root: "Everything in this section is a function of the pair (polygon, root)"). Since the Lean quantifies over every n ≥ 3, every representative P, and every pair g h : ZMod n, every polygon, every representative of it, and every pair of its edges is covered. Non-vacuous: any nondegenerate triangle satisfies G1 and G2, and convex polygons in general position do for every n ≥ 4.

Generic P := G1 P ∧ G2 P. `G1 P := ∀ i j k, i ≠ j → j ≠ k → i ≠ k → chi P i j k ≠ 0` with `chi P i j k := sign (det (P j − P i) (P k − P i))`, `det u v := u.1*v.2 − u.2*v.1`; this is verbatim def:chirotope χ_ijk(P) = sgn det(μ_j − μ_i, μ_k − μ_i) and (G1) "χ_ijk(P) ≠ 0 for all pairwise distinct i,j,k". `G2 P := ¬∃ i j k x, i≠j ∧ j≠k ∧ i≠k ∧ x ∈ edgeInterior P i ∧ ... k` with `edgeInterior P i = {x | ∃ t, 0<t ∧ t<1 ∧ x = P i + t•(P(i+1) − P i)}`, i.e. the relative interior of the segment E_i = [μ_i, μ_{i+1}] (for a nondegenerate segment; for a degenerate one both sides give the single point). The printed (G2) speaks of "three distinct edge segments" while Lean uses three distinct indices; under G1 with n ≥ 3 all vertices are distinct (lem:g1(i), Lean `g1_vertices_injective`), so E_i = E_j as sets forces {i,i+1} = {j,j+1}, i.e. i = j (n = 2 excluded). Hence within Generic = G1 ∧ G2 the two readings are equivalent; Generic is neither stronger nor weaker than printed "generic".

(b) "any two of its edges g,h". def:root: a root is an edge, on a representative an edge index g ∈ ℤ/n, root edge E_g from μ_g to μ_{g+1}. Lean: `(g h : ZMod n)`, and ZMod n = Fin n for n ≥ 1. Identical range (including g = h, harmless).

(c) "A_g(P)" = `treeCoefficient P hP.1 g hn`. Expansion: `boundaryIndex g k = g + k + 1` for k : Fin n, so `boundaryWord P g k = P (g+k+1)`: a_0 = μ_{g+1}, ..., a_{n−1} = μ_{g+n} = μ_g — exactly def:root's boundary word for the root E_g (the omitted edge is E_g from μ_g to μ_{g+1}; leaf E_{g+k} joins a_{k−1}, a_k, cf. `boundaryWord_leaf_edge`). `BoundaryInterval n` = {left < right in Fin n} = intervals [i,j], 0 ≤ i < j ≤ N = n−1, `leaves = right − left` = j − i. `IntervalComposition I` = (parts s > 0, strictly monotone cut : Fin (s+1) → Fin n with cut 0 = i, cut s = j) = (r_0 < ... < r_s), r_0 = i, r_s = j, s ≥ 1; `part k` = [r_k, r_{k+1}]. Gates (def:gates): `nearSign π P g k = chi P a_{r_{k+2}} a_{r_{k+1}} a_{r_k}` for k : Fin (s−1) (printed index k+1 ∈ 1..s−1) = χ(a_{r_{K+1}}, a_{r_K}, a_{r_{K−1}}) = d_K, since chi P i j k = χ(μ_i, μ_j, μ_k) with χ(x,y,z) = sgn det(y−x, z−x); `farSign = chi P a_j a_{r_K} a_i` = χ(a_j, a_{r_K}, a_i) = h_K. `signTheta s _ = if s = 1 then 1 else 0` agrees with Θ on ±1 (Θ(1) = 1, Θ(−1) = 0 is forced by the lem:gates-nonzero identities dΘ(−hd) = (d−h)/2, dΘ(hd) = (d+h)/2). `ordinaryGate d h = d·Θ(−h·d)`, `rootGate d h = d·Θ(h·d)`; `ordinaryWeight = ∏_{k<s−1} ordinaryGate(d_k,h_k)` = V^+(π), `rootWeight` = V^−(π), empty product 1 when s = 1 (matches "V^±(π) = 1 when s = 1"). `openTreeRec`: 1 if leaves = 1, else −∑_{π, 2 ≤ parts} V^+(π) ∏_parts openTreeRec — verbatim the b_{[i,j]} recursion (leaves ≥ 1 always, so "≠ 1" is "≥ 2"). `treeCoefficient P hP g hn = rootedTreeRec ... (fullBoundaryInterval hn)` with fullBoundaryInterval = [0, n−1] = [0,N], and `rootedTreeRec = ∑_{all π} rootWeight(π) ∏_k openTreeRec(part k)` = ∑_π V^−(π) ∏ b_parts including the one-part composition (weight 1, term b_{[0,N]}) — verbatim A_g(P). Values in ℤ as printed. The proof arguments `hP.1 : G1 P` and `hn` enter only in Prop positions (`signTheta` ignores its proof; Fin bounds of fullBoundaryInterval), so by proof irrelevance the value does not depend on which proofs are supplied; `hP.1` is the (G1) component of Generic, which is exactly what def:treesum requires ("Let P satisfy (G1)").

Root convention / shift: `shift k P i = P (i+k)`, so shift 1 = σ ((σP)_i = μ_{i+1}) and the physical root g of P is root g − a of shift a P, matching def:root ("the shift carries the root g of P to the root g−1 of σP"); the library records this as `treeCoefficient_shift : treeCoefficient (shift a P) _ (g − a) hn = treeCoefficient P hP g hn`. For this theorem it is immaterial: both sides are evaluated on the same representative P with root indices g, h on that representative, and (P, g, h) are universally quantified, so for any polygon, any representative, and any two physical edges the corresponding instance is present. Well-definedness of A_g on the orbit is not a clause of thm:root-indep-proof.
